loadTimeline.method: 60 fps resample of the retained 1280x576 recording (scaled 640x288): whole-frame mean, card region mean, bottom-right spinner max; converted to phone wall residue as onsetPhoneWallLow16 + (video time - HUD first), assuming the helper onset and the video's first HUD frame are the same event; +-17 ms
loadTimeline.sequence: dial screen -> '12:00 AM 7th Night' card -> black -> black with a loading spinner -> first office frame
loadTimeline.reading: All three nights run the same sequence within ~30 ms of their Start taps up to the spinner; the first office frame lands 5013-5091 ms after the tap, the spread accumulating during loading (spinner 1433-1483 ms). A and B's onset residues are 62 ms apart.

facts: CRunFrame.loadFullFrame sets m_wRandomSeed = -1 and replaces it only from a frame seed chunk
CRun.allocRunHeader: m_wRandomSeed == -1 -> rh3Graine = (short) System.currentTimeMillis(); CRun.random is rh3Graine = rh3Graine * 31415 + 1 & 0xFFFF
callers: CRunApp.startTheFrame -> new CRun -> initRunLoop -> allocRunHeader (after loadFullFrame); CRun.doRunLoop -> allocRunHeader
CND_EVERY2 is a countdown advanced by CRun.rhTimerDelta (currentTimeMillis differences) only when evaluated
seedMomentFromRuntime.reading: Every frame start reseeds from the phone clock, so launch time cannot matter. The office frame seeds at the end of its loading, just before its first frame is built and drawn (see pinned).

callOrder: CRunApp.startTheFrame: new CRunFrame -> loadFullFrame -> (screen zoom, collision masks, layer effects) -> new CRun -> initRunLoop -> followToFades
CRunFrame.loadFullFrame loads the frame's heavy data: COIList.load, CSoundBank.load, CMusicBank.load, CImageBank.load, CFontBank.load (the black-with-spinner stretch)

CRun.initRunLoop: allocRunHeader FIRST (the clock seed), then initAsmLoop, y_InitLevel, prepareFrame, createFrameObjects, redrawLevel, loadGlobalObjectsData, event program prepare/assemble, f_InitLoop
pinned.instant: the office frame's seed is taken after all of its loading finishes and before its objects are created and first drawn: at the end of the spinner, a short roughly constant delay before the first office frame the helper stamps as onset (expected under ~100 ms, not measured)

encounters.tool: eyehole-read.py, windows release + 1.0 + 10 c s, 2.6 s at 5 fps, release = HUD first + 2.433 - 0.070 s

readerCheck.method: contact sheet of twin A built from eyehole-read.py's own decode (frames(video, startS, 2.6, 5)), tile = the reader's bestFrame, occupant pixel count recomputed on that exact frame (42/42 equal to the reader's), measured region boxed and enlarged
readerCheck.result: 12 Withered Chica and 12 Withered Bonnie labels show that animatronic in the eyehole; 15 empty labels show only the mask rim; cycles 22 and 36 (Withered Freddy) show a brown-orange torn face, an animatronic whose identity is plausible but not confirmed by eye; cycle 20 (unlabelled) is Chica mid-motion at the region edge
readerCheck.correction: An earlier statement in this session that ~1 in 7 eyehole labels are wrong (from the 12/14 hallfix calibration) does not describe this night and is withdrawn as the explanation for the seed scores. A first check sheet that re-seeked the video instead of using the reader's decode showed mismatched frames; that sheet was wrong, not the reader.
readerCheck.limit: the window covers 2.6 s per cycle, so an empty read can miss an encounter; misses are not counted as conflicts

pairs.method: jointly identified = both runs read a Withered identity that cycle; disagreements count different identities and identified-vs-empty

modelSeedScores.model: k3 at epoch 2433 with sourcedRouteForks + sourcedDropLightOrder + sourcedFoxyChain (lit counter, commit 64cd7c5), constructor draw undone; all 65,536 seeds; conflicts = different identity or read identity the model lacks

nearMomentBestRank.note: best rank among the 121 seeds within +-60 ms of each moment; a random 121 gives ~540

modelSeedScores.reading: No moment ranks well for both nights and no seed sits in both nights' top 200. The eyehole labels are not the cause (see readerCheck): the best model seeds still conflict with correct reads on 3 (A) and 4 (B) cycles, so the model's encounter sequence or the assumed seed moment is still wrong.

constantOffsetScan.method: seed residue = onset residue + d for d in -300..+100 ms; rank of that seed per night (k3 run 1 onset 17592, A 25097, B 25035); joint score = sum of log(rank/65536); null = the same best-over-offsets score for 40 random onset triples
constantOffsetScan.reading: No single offset ranks all three nights well; the best joint score is carried by B alone and sits at the edge of what random onsets reach. With the reads verified correct on A, the limit is the model's encounter prediction (or the seed-moment assumption), not the observable's labels.

byRule.twinSupport: not met: A and B agree on 0 of 12 jointly identified cycles (needs all of at least 8)
byRule.twinRefutation: not met: A and B disagree on 12 of 12, but their onset residues are 62 ms apart (the rule needs <= 50 ms)

verdict.reading: The twins could not share a seed: the seed is taken at the end of the office frame's loading, and the nights' clocks there differed by tens of milliseconds, from loading jitter the Start tap cannot control. A and B agree less than either agrees with the control (C), as expected for three unrelated seeds. The design cannot force a seed; it can only locate the seed moment.

conclusions: k3 won all three counted twin nights (A, B, C): with k3 run 1, four wins in four phone nights; not a rate.
The timed Start tap lands within 0-47 ms of its planned phone wall-clock residue.

The office frame reseeds from the phone clock after its loading finishes (decompiled call order), 5.0-5.1 s after the Start tap, with tens of ms of loading jitter, so same-residue taps do not give the same seed.

Eyehole labels on A are correct by eye; the best fixed-model seeds still conflict with correct reads on 3 (A), 4 (B) and 6 (C) cycles, so the model's encounter sequence or the seed-moment assumption remains wrong.
No constant seed-to-onset offset ranks the nights' seeds well beyond chance.
